description: Bonjour à tous ! 👋 Je m'appelle N'Dri Moahe Othniel, étudiant en informatique et passionné de sciences et de technologies. Convaincu que l'espace est l'une des plus grandes frontières de l'humanité, je souhaite, à travers le NASA Space Apps Challenge, mettre mes compétences et ma créativité au service de l'innovation.
summary: A.S.T.R.A. Space helps astronauts on long-duration missions understand their exercise results and follow an individually approved training plan. An onboard station compares each crew member’s completed sessions with their own targets. It supports records modeled on the resistance, treadmill, and cycling equipment used on the International Space Station. When enough comparable sessions are available, the system can propose a bounded adjustment for human review. The companion app displays the approved plan, explains results, and lets the astronaut send a concern to the onboard team. Nova, a virtual cat, grows as sessions are confirmed and offers play, family photos, and reminders during rest periods. The current prototype was tested in a browser with synthetic session records and a knowledge base built from published NASA resources.
details:
Exercise data is most useful when a crew member can see what changed, understand why it matters to their own plan, and act on an approved next step. A.S.T.R.A. Space brings that workflow to an onboard station and a personal companion app.

The Python and FastAPI backend stores exercise records and individual plans in SQLite. Its data model supports sessions for ARED, T2, and CEVIS, including equipment-specific measures such as load and repetitions, speed, or power and cadence. It compares comparable sessions against goals and limits set for the individual. Incomplete or questionable records prompt review. When the evidence supports an adjustment, the analysis records the observations behind the proposal. A specialist and the mission lead review the proposed change before release.

The scientific knowledge base is a JSON collection of published NASA material on exercise, human performance, medical operations, and crew health records. Each entry identifies the source and distinguishes its published findings from the team’s interpretation. The individual exercise target comes from the crew member’s approved plan. Groq can explain station results through guided questions, while the station keeps control of the figures and the approved plan. A local response is available when the external service is unavailable.

The companion was built with Expo, React Native, and TypeScript. It shows session history, explains the comparison with the individual target, displays the approved plan, and lets the astronaut send a concern to the onboard team. Nova grows with confirmed sessions and gives the astronaut a familiar activity during rest periods through play and personal photos. The intended benefit is to make follow-up easier to understand and sustain when access to ground support is limited.

We verified the browser workflow with synthetic records. The release still needs a unified station-to-app data path, verified equipment imports, and an end-to-end test on physical phones before a ground-based pilot.
